definitions.gloss: acquaintance, someone whose face you know
definitions.explanation: A person you recognize by sight and may greet, but don't know well; someone between a stranger and a friend.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}とは{顔見知|かおみし}り{程度|ていど}の{関係|かんけい}だ。
examples.english: He and I are just acquaintances.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}に{顔見知|かおみし}りが{増|ふ}えてきた。
examples.english: I've gotten to know more people in the neighborhood by sight.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}で{顔見知|かおみし}りに{会|あ}って{挨拶|あいさつ}した。
examples.english: I ran into an acquaintance at the station and greeted them.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}というより{顔見知|かおみし}りだ。
examples.english: They're more of an acquaintance than a friend.

notes:
{顔見知|かおみし}り describes someone you recognize but don't know well.

ETYMOLOGY:
{顔|かお} (face) + {見知|みし}り (from {見知|みし}る, to come to know by sight) - someone whose face you have come to know.

USAGE NOTE:
Implies a limited relationship - you might nod or say hello when you see them, but you wouldn't socialize or share personal matters. Often used to describe neighbors, regular customers, or people from the same school/workplace you don't interact with closely.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {顔見知|かおみし}り{程度|ていど} - just an acquaintance (emphasizes the limited nature)
- {顔見知|かおみし}りになる - to become acquaintances

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {顔見知|かおみし}り vs. {知|し}り{合|あ}い: Similar meaning, but {顔見知|かおみし}り emphasizes recognizing by face; {知|し}り{合|あ}い can include people you know by name/reputation
- {顔見知|かおみし}り vs. {友達|ともだち}: {顔見知|かおみし}り is more distant than {友達|ともだち}
